prompt:
Use the attached image as the reference: the same woman — the personification of Fermium (Fm) — seen off duty in her everyday life. Keep her face, eye colour, hair colour, skin tone and body exactly; change only her clothes, pose and place. Do not reuse earlier conversation images.

Output: one vertical 2:3 image, 1024×1536.

Face: exactly the attached image's face — the same short midface and face length-to-width ratio; the camera angle, pose, bangs or a headpiece never make her face look longer or her jaw heavier.

Style: A Japanese anime key visual with a painterly finish: an anime-style character with an elegant adult anime face, large expressive eyes, a small nose and mouth, fine coloured linework and soft cel-to-painted shading with painted highlights in the hair and fabric. Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance. No flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face or plastic 3D-render finish. Keep this rendering exactly as in the attached image — the same finish, line, shading, skin and colour treatment.

Place: a chemistry laboratory with a long worktable of glass flasks, a fume hood and shelves of labelled reagent bottles
Time of day: dawn — the first pale light, cool and quiet, the sky just turning; the first pale light at the window, the room still dim.
Hair: her hair tied up in a loose bun or ponytail — same colour and length as the attached image, a few strands loose.
Light direction: dappled light — patches of light with leaf or blind shadow across her.
Outfit: a ballet leotard with a short wrap skirt, tights and leg warmers — in graphite grey with black trim; the outfit colour reads clearly at first glance; styled with close-fitting ribbed fabric, a shirt tied around the waist by its sleeves and a few thin stacked bangles on one wrist; right now — one strap — or one side of the neckline — has slipped down off her shoulder, baring that whole shoulder and the top of her arm; she leaves it as it is, worn with maximal styling presence — the chosen outfit worn in its most revealing version — a deep neckline with natural cleavage, bare shoulders, a cropped or open-back cut, a short hem or high slit showing the thighs, as far as the outfit allows, skin clearly showing, following her curvy figure — a slim waist and rounded hips; intimate areas covered.
POSTURE: crouching low on her heels.
COMPOSITION: a full-body shot, her complete head, hands and feet inside the frame with restrained margins; body in side profile, her face in profile too, not turned toward the camera, facing the left of the frame, so her own left side is toward the camera; camera slightly above, looking down at her; she is placed in the left third of the frame, open space of the place to her right; a wall or backdrop of the place close behind her.
Lens / perspective: 35mm-equivalent environmental perspective balancing the woman and the setting with moderate depth.
RIGHT HAND: her own right hand rests on her knee — her far arm, on the side away from the camera.
LEFT HAND: her own left hand rests naturally for the posture, relaxed and empty — her near arm, on the camera side.
LEGS: crouched on the balls of her feet, knees bent.
GAZE: her eyes are lowered.
EXPRESSION: one brow raised higher, eyes wide and attentive, lips slightly parted.

Leave behind everything she wears in the attached image — no crown, tiara, helmet, feathers, headpiece, hairpins from it, armour or regalia; her hair is styled for the everyday outfit, with at most one small accessory.

Her element — fermium: element 100, the first to reach three digits, found together with her twin einsteinium in the fallout of the first hydrogen-bomb test in 1952, and named for the physicist who lit the first nuclear reactor, a pile of graphite blocks stacked in a squash court beneath the stands of a university sports field in the winter of 1942; she is the end of the road for building heavier elements by feeding neutrons to a reactor, because the next step splits apart almost at once, a wall no neutron can climb; her longest-lived form lasts only about a hundred days, and no one has ever gathered enough of her to see — may show in the outfit's details, motifs or small accessories.

Figure: keep her exact build from the attached image, neither slimmer nor fuller.

Light: the place's own light, lit and coloured the way this style renders light and skin.

One figure in focus, natural hands with five fingers, no text or numbers other than her element's own symbol and atomic number, no logo or watermark. No animals or other creatures.
